extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, Scientific Review Officers, and NIH extramural staff involved in research grant peer review
extracted.subtask_description: Official NIH guidance on how research grant and cooperative agreement applications are reviewed, scored, and processed at both the initial Scientific Review Group (study section) level and the Institute/Center Advisory Council/Board level. Includes roles, criteria, scoring, appeals, and post-review procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core values of peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Peer review is driven by core values to seek the highest level of ethical standards and to promote a process that strives to be fair, equitable, timely, and free of bias.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These core values form the foundation for the laws, regulations, and policies that govern the NIH peer review process and should inform all conduct by reviewers, SROs, and NIH staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dual peer review system (first and second level review)
rubrics_metrics.description: The NIH uses a dual peer review system: first-level review by a Scientific Review Group (SRG/study section) and second-level review by Institute/Center National Advisory Councils or Boards.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only applications recommended for approval by both the SRG and the Advisory Council may be recommended for funding; final funding decisions are made by IC Directors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scientific Review Officer responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: The SRO is responsible for ensuring each application receives an objective and fair initial peer review and that applicable laws, regulations, and policies are followed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: SRO duties include analyzing application content and completeness, documenting/managing conflicts of interest, recruiting qualified reviewers (authority in field, dedication to fair reviews, collegiality, review experience, balanced representation), assigning applications, overseeing administrative/regulatory aspects of meetings, and preparing summary statements.

rubrics_metrics.name: SRG Chair role
rubrics_metrics.description: Serves as moderator of the discussion of scientific and technical merit of applications under review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Also serves as a peer reviewer for the meeting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewer duties and responsibilities
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers must declare conflicts of interest, maintain confidentiality, prepare written critiques for assigned applications, assign numerical scores to each scored review criterion, and make recommendations concerning scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers receive access to applications ~6 weeks prior, follow SRO directions on critique preparation, recommend protections for human subjects, inclusion, vertebrate animal welfare, biohazards, and advise on budget appropriateness. See NIH guidance pages on conflicts, integrity/confidentiality, and human/animal protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicant conduct regarding peer review integrity
rubrics_metrics.description: Applicants must not contact reviewers to influence outcomes, must not send information directly to a reviewer, and must not access review-related information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Violations have consequences; applicants should consult 'Integrity and Confidentiality in NIH Peer Review'.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact (scored)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers provide an overall impact score reflecting the likelihood the project will exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research fields involved, considering the scored review criteria and applicable additional criteria.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers give a preliminary overall impact score before the meeting; final impact scores are given by eligible committee members after discussion and reflect evaluation of overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Significance is one of the five scored review criteria used to evaluate research grant and cooperative agreement applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance is considered in determining scientific and technical merit and the overall impact score (detailed description of what constitutes significance is provided in 'Review Criteria at a Glance').

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigator(s) (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigator(s) is a scored criterion assessing the qualifications, experience, and suitability of the project team.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluated alongside other scored criteria to inform the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Innovation (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Innovation is a scored criterion assessing the novelty and originality of concepts, approaches, or technologies proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in relation to potential to shift current research paradigms and contribute to impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approach (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Approach is a scored criterion evaluating the rigor, feasibility, and appropriateness of the research design and methods.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers assess methodology, analysis plans, and potential weaknesses; Approach scores strongly influence overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Environment (scored review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Environment is a scored criterion assessing the institutional support, resources, and facilities that will contribute to project success.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes evaluation of whether the setting is conducive to productive research and career development, where applicable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Study Timeline (additional review criterion, clinical trials-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications involving clinical trials, reviewers will evaluate the study timeline as an additional criterion while determining scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This item does not receive a separate score but informs the overall impact evaluation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate protections for human subjects as applicable to the project, though this item is not given a separate numeric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should consider risks, safeguards, and compliance with human subjects regulations when making overall impact judgments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of Women, Minorities, and Children (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers assess plans and justification for inclusion (or exclusion) of women, minorities, and children in clinical research when applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This affects overall merit determinations but is not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate welfare and ethical use of vertebrate animals as applicable to the application.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations can affect funding and progression; not separately scored but considered in overall impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (additional review criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers evaluate the presence of biohazards and adequacy of protections where applicable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Considered in overall impact scoring; serious biohazard issues may lead to NRFC.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmission, Renewal, Revision (additional review criteria)
rubrics_metrics.description: When applicable, reviewers will evaluate resubmissions, renewals, and revisions as additional items in determining scientific and technical merit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These items inform overall impact but are not given separate numeric scores; prior review history and changes can be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applications from Foreign Organizations (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should consider applications from foreign organizations as applicable, but this item is not scored and should not be used in providing overall impact scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Indicated as an item to consider separately from scored criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Select Agent considerations (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Presence of select agents must be considered as an additional, non-scored item during review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concerns here may affect fundability and compliance, but are not separately scored.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resource Sharing Plans (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Resource sharing plans (data, model organisms, etc.) are considered by reviewers though not given separate scores.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Adequacy of sharing plans should be noted but should not be used in calculating the overall impact score.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological/ Chemical Resources (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers should consider plans for authentication of key biological and chemical resources; this is not separately scored.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important for reproducibility and reliability; considered in overall merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period Support (additional review consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers consider whether the requested budget and period of support are reasonable and appropriate, but should not use this consideration in determining overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers may make recommendations concerning appropriateness of budget requests; program staff and grants management handle final budget decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: NIH numeric scoring system (9-point scale) and score calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: NIH uses a 9-point rating scale (1 = exceptional; 9 = poor) for overall impact and criterion scores. Final overall impact score is the mean of eligible members' final impact scores multiplied by 10, producing values from 10 (high impact) to 90 (low impact).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before meetings reviewers give separate scores for each of at least five criteria and a preliminary overall impact score. Preliminary scores may be used to triage which applications are discussed. Applications not discussed are reported as ND and typically do not receive numeric impact scores.

rubrics_metrics.name: Not Recommended for Further Consideration (NRFC) designation
rubrics_metrics.description: An application may be designated NRFC by the SRG if it lacks significant and substantial merit; presents serious ethical problems in protection of human subjects; or presents serious ethical problems in vertebrate animals, biohazards, and/or select agents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NRFC applications do not proceed to second-level review because they cannot be funded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Summary Statement content and ND designation
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications not discussed receive the designation 'ND' (may be reported as ++) on the summary statement; assigned reviewers' written comments and criterion scores are still provided to the applicant and NIH staff as feedback.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The summary statement shows reviewer critiques and scores for each scored review criterion and identifies the base used to determine any percentile.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understanding and reporting percentiles
rubrics_metrics.description: A percentile approximates the percentage of applications that received a better overall impact score from the study section during the past year; percentiles are reported as whole numbers and only a subset of applications receive percentiles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Different bases may be used for ad hoc study sections; the summary statement will identify the base used. Percentiles vary across ICs and application types.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appeals policy and allowable grounds for appeal
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators may appeal initial review results if they believe the review process was flawed due to reviewer bias, conflict of interest, absence of appropriate expertise, or factual errors that could have substantially altered the review outcome.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Policy NOT applicable to appeals of R&D contract technical evaluations, NIH funding decisions, or decisions about MERIT award extensions; see NOT-OD-11-064 for details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Second-level review considerations and recommendation process
rubrics_metrics.description: Advisory Council/Board members and NIH program staff examine overall impact scores, percentile rankings (if any), and summary statements in light of the IC's priorities to advise on funding decisions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Program staff provide a grant-funding plan to Council; Council conducts special reviews (e.g., for investigators with $1M+ direct costs) and considers IC goals before advising the IC Director, who makes final funding decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Post-review 'next steps' and resubmission guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: If not funded, applicants may resubmit addressing reviewer concerns or submit a new application; summary statements direct applicants to 'Next Steps' and to contact assigned program officials for guidance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If fundable, ICs may publish paylines and funding strategies; applicants should compare scores to paylines for the fiscal year of funding consideration and consult program officials about likelihood of funding and administrative steps if awarded.
